units.text: The canonical Linear vocabulary for Projects and tickets.

Status records where work is now and which role is at work; Type records why a ticket exists and who holds it; Mode records how a captain works with the user; Severity records how serious the finding behind a ticket is; Priority records which of the user's tickets comes next.

notRule.note: what each of Status, Type, Mode, Severity, Priority records

units.text: The model is supersymmetric: a captain's ticket is a Project one level down, and the same statuses, Types and chain hold at both levels.

notRule.note: supersymmetry; the same statuses, Types and chain hold at both levels

units.text: The order of the statuses is part of the standard: Linear draws each status circle from its position in its category.

rules.rule: The order of the statuses is part of the standard: Ticket statuses keep the listed order so Linear draws each status circle from its position in its category.

units.text: | `Backlog` | A possible Project retained for later; no one has started charting it. |

rules.rule: Project status `Backlog` means a possible Project retained for later that no one has started charting.

units.text: | `Planning` | The map holder is charting the first low-resolution map with `wayfinder`; a repository plan, when one is written, runs its review loop. |

rules.rule: Project status `Planning` means the map holder is charting the first low-resolution map with `wayfinder`, and any repository plan written runs its review loop.

units.text: | `Planned` | The user approved the charted route, and any repository plan passed independent review; the map holder commissions the first Ticket Captain to open the feature. |

rules.rule: Project status `Planned` means the user approved the charted route and any repository plan passed independent review; the map holder then commissions the first Ticket Captain to open the feature.

units.text: | `In Progress` | The map holder is working the map through Ticket Captains toward the destination. |

rules.rule: Project status `In Progress` means the map holder is working the map through Ticket Captains toward the destination.

units.text: | `Completed` | The destination landed and the landing's walkthrough found nothing more; commission [spec retirement](./feature-spec-convention.md#retirement). |

rules.rule: Project status `Completed` means the destination landed and the landing walkthrough found nothing more; the map holder then commissions spec retirement.

units.text: | `Canceled` | The destination was consciously abandoned; record why and commission [spec retirement](./feature-spec-convention.md#retirement). |

rules.rule: Project status `Canceled` means the destination was consciously abandoned; the map holder records why and commissions spec retirement.

units.text: There are no canonical Project labels: a Project's status and ticket graph carry the information.

rules.rule: A Project carries no canonical labels; its status and ticket graph carry the information.

units.text: One set for primary tickets and Sub-tickets alike, ten statuses in Linear's categories and in this order.

rules.rule: Primary tickets and Sub-tickets share one set of ten statuses, in Linear's categories and in the listed order.

units.text: The captain alone sets a delivery ticket's status; the record that runs the chain flips on every chain spawn, and nothing else flips it.

rules.rule: The captain alone sets a delivery ticket's status.
The record that runs the chain flips status on every chain spawn, and nothing else flips it.

units.text: | `FutureFeature` | backlog | An unscheduled strategic possibility with no Type yet. Only the user promotes it. |

rules.rule: Status `FutureFeature` (backlog) is an unscheduled strategic possibility with no Type yet.
Only the user promotes a `FutureFeature`.

units.text: | `Backlog` | backlog | Retained with a Type, unscheduled, waiting to become a Todo: no contract yet, or one awaiting the user's go, as an Inquisition's. |

rules.rule: Status `Backlog` (backlog) holds a ticket retained with a Type, unscheduled and waiting to become a Todo: no contract yet, or one awaiting the user's go, as an Inquisition's.

units.text: | `Todo` | unstarted | The incoming list: contracted and to be started soon. An open native blocker still prevents pickup. A `Question` in `Todo` is the user's turn. |

rules.rule: Status `Todo` (unstarted) is the incoming list: contracted tickets to be started soon.
An open native blocker prevents pickup of a `Todo` ticket.
A `Question` in `Todo` is the user's turn.

units.text: | `In Progress` | started | A record not running the chain itself: a parent while its lanes run, a wayfinding ticket, an Inquisition's sweep (its map, phases, triage and patch lane) until its record enters the chain. |

rules.rule: Status `In Progress` (started) is for a record not running the chain itself: a parent while its lanes run, a wayfinding ticket, an Inquisition's sweep (map, phases, triage, patch lane) until its record enters the chain.

units.text: | `Implementing` | started | The author of the change's kind is spawned for one hop - a `code-writer`, or a `docs-writer` for a documentation change - a fix hop after a FAIL included. |

rules.rule: Status `Implementing` (started) is set when the author of the change's kind is spawned for one hop - a `code-writer`, or a `docs-writer` for a documentation change - a fix hop after a FAIL included.

units.text: | `In Review` | started | Any reviewer is spawned, the optional spec review of the contract before any code included. A FAIL, one or more blockers, returns the record to `Implementing`; a spec review returns it there on either verdict. |

rules.rule: Status `In Review` (started) is set when any reviewer is spawned, the optional spec review of the contract before any code included.
A review FAIL (one or more blockers) returns the record to `Implementing`.
A spec review returns the record to `Implementing` on either verdict.

units.text: | `Ready to Merge` | started | The PR carries its PASS block and waits for its merge turn. The record stays here while its own Merge Sub-ticket runs; the landing, one Project at a time, and an atomic ticket wait here for the user's click. A merge review FAIL that reverts sends it back to `Implementing`. |

rules.rule: Status `Ready to Merge` (started) means the PR carries its PASS block and waits for its merge turn.
The record stays `Ready to Merge` while its own Merge Sub-ticket runs.
The landing (one Project at a time) and an atomic ticket wait in `Ready to Merge` for the user's click.
A merge review FAIL that reverts sends the record back to `Implementing`.

units.text: | `Done` | completed | Merged, or the outcome the Type names reached, with its evidence. |

rules.rule: Status `Done` (completed) means merged, or the outcome the Type names reached, with its evidence.

units.text: | `Canceled` | canceled | The ticket will not be completed; the record says why. |

rules.rule: Status `Canceled` (canceled) means the ticket will not be completed; the record says why.

units.text: | `Duplicate` | canceled | Another ticket owns the outcome; the record links to it. |

rules.rule: Status `Duplicate` (canceled) means another ticket owns the outcome; the record links to it.

units.text: `Ready to Merge` holds for a lane into its parent, a primary into the feature branch, and an atomic ticket or the landing into main; a Merge Sub-ticket never enters it, since it runs the chain and closes.

rules.rule: `Ready to Merge` holds for a lane into its parent, a primary into the feature branch, and an atomic ticket or the landing into main.
A Merge Sub-ticket never enters `Ready to Merge`: it runs the chain and closes.

units.text: `In Review` on the board always means a reviewer is running.

rules.rule: `In Review` on the board always means a reviewer is running.

units.text: A ticket with an open native blocker is blocked in any status; do not add a `Blocked` status that can drift from Linear's dependency graph.

rules.rule: A ticket with an open native blocker is blocked in any status.
Do not add a `Blocked` status; it can drift from Linear's dependency graph.

units.text: Assignment is the claim: assigned means taken; unassigned, `Todo` and unblocked means pickable.

rules.rule: Assignment is the claim: an assigned ticket is taken; an unassigned, `Todo`, unblocked ticket is pickable.

units.text: A `FutureFeature` is promoted by the user alone: at ticket grain it gains a Type and moves to `Backlog` or `Todo` on the same record; at Project or Initiative grain that record is created and linked and the FutureFeature is marked `Done`.

rules.rule: Only the user promotes a `FutureFeature`.
At ticket grain, promoting a `FutureFeature` gives it a Type and moves it to `Backlog` or `Todo` on the same record.
At Project or Initiative grain, promoting a `FutureFeature` creates and links that record and marks the FutureFeature `Done`.

units.text: A rejected one becomes `Canceled` with the reason recorded.

rules.rule: A rejected `FutureFeature` becomes `Canceled` with the reason recorded.

units.text: Three label groups, `Type`, `Mode` and `Severity`, because one label per group is the rule Linear enforces.

rules.rule: Tickets use three label groups, `Type`, `Mode` and `Severity`, one label per group (the rule Linear enforces).

units.text: Every ticket carries exactly one Type.

rules.rule: Every ticket carries exactly one Type.

units.text: Mode sits on every Type a captain holds.

rules.rule: Mode sits on every Type a captain holds.

units.text: Severity sits only on a ticket born from a finding.

rules.rule: Severity sits only on a ticket born from a finding.

units.text: | `Feature` | captain | any | Add, improve, refactor or document: an outcome to build. | the outcome merged | `#BB87FC` |

rules.rule: Type `Feature` is held by a captain, at any level: add, improve, refactor or document an outcome to build; it closes on the outcome merged.

units.text: | `Bug` | captain | any | Restore intended behaviour. The record holds the defect and its fix. | the behaviour restored | `#EB5757` |

rules.rule: Type `Bug` is held by a captain, at any level: restore intended behaviour, the record holding the defect and its fix; it closes on the behaviour restored.

units.text: | `Merge` | captain | any; the landing is the only primary one | One merge operation: lanes into a parent, a primary into the feature, the feature into main. | the merge review PASS | `#4EA7FC` |

rules.rule: Type `Merge` is held by a captain at any level (the landing is the only primary one): one merge operation (lanes into a parent, a primary into the feature, the feature into main); it closes on the merge review PASS.

units.text: | `Enablement` | captain | any | Access, environment, credentials or material other work needs; `wizard` guides the steps only the user can do. | the condition true, with evidence | `#26B5CE` |

rules.rule: Type `Enablement` is held by a captain at any level: access, environment, credentials or material other work needs; it closes on the condition true, with evidence.
`wizard` guides the steps of an Enablement that only the user can do.

units.text: | `Inquisition` | captain | primary; its group Sub-tickets above about 10 areas | One round of audit of the integrated feature: an area map, each area run through Read, Break and Drive by `inquisitor` crew, every finding triaged by severity into Bugs, one nit ticket and Questions. Each round starts from zero. | its record merged and verified on the feature, Bugs filed and their proof refs retained; a group Sub-ticket, its register final and pushed | `#5E6AD2` |

rules.rule: Type `Inquisition` is held by a captain, on a primary ticket, with group Sub-tickets above about 10 areas: one round of audit of the integrated feature (area map, each area run through Read, Break and Drive by `inquisitor` crew, every finding triaged by severity into Bugs, one nit ticket and Questions), each round starting from zero.
An Inquisition closes when its record is merged and verified on the feature, Bugs filed and their proof refs retained; a group Sub-ticket closes when its register is final and pushed.

units.text: | `Prototype` | captain | any | A design question raised to fidelity the user can react to; fast sketches, the user is the review. | the user's verdict on the ticket | `#F2994A` |

rules.rule: Type `Prototype` is held by a captain at any level: a design question raised to fidelity the user can react to, fast sketches, the user being the review; it closes on the user's verdict on the ticket.

units.text: | `Question` | map holder | any | One prepared, discrete question whose answer blocks named work. | the user's answer on the ticket | `#F2C94C` |

rules.rule: Type `Question` is held by the map holder at any level: one prepared, discrete question whose answer blocks named work; it closes on the user's answer on the ticket.

units.text: | `Research` | map holder | any | A factual answer whose investigation needs its own owner, status or evidence. | cited findings on the ticket | `#95A2B3` |

rules.rule: Type `Research` is held by the map holder at any level: a factual answer whose investigation needs its own owner, status or evidence; it closes on cited findings on the ticket.

units.text: | `Grilling` | map holder | any | A tree of intent or specification choices resolved with the user. | shared understanding recorded, with its Decision Records linked | `#D4A017` |

rules.rule: Type `Grilling` is held by the map holder at any level: a tree of intent or specification choices resolved with the user; it closes on shared understanding recorded, with its Decision Records linked.

units.text: | `Walkthrough` | map holder | primary only | The user walks the whole product as it stands: the feature branch at a Milestone, or main at the landing. The emphasis is on what changed since the last walkthrough and what needs the most careful look. The tour also covers where to look, how to try it, and what reviewers left open. There's one per Milestone, prepared even if he skips it, and the landing's comes last. | his verdict quoted on the ticket, or his skip recorded; findings filed as tickets | `#C69C6D` |

rules.rule: Type `Walkthrough` is held by the map holder on a primary ticket only: the user walks the whole product as it stands (the feature branch at a Milestone, or main at the landing); it closes on his verdict quoted on the ticket, or his skip recorded, findings filed as tickets.
A Walkthrough emphasizes what changed since the last walkthrough and what needs the most careful look, and covers where to look, how to try it, and what reviewers left open.
There is one Walkthrough per Milestone, prepared even if the user skips it, and the landing's comes last.

units.text: A captain-held ticket normally uses one author - `code-writer`, or `docs-writer` for a documentation change - and review at the working-tree standard's [Delivery scale](../guides/working-tree-standard.md#delivery-scale-and-evidence).

rules.rule: A captain-held ticket normally uses one author - `code-writer`, or `docs-writer` for a documentation change - and review at the working-tree standard's Delivery scale.

units.text: A spec review of the contract before any code needs one short concrete risk reason, recorded in the contract; persistence, migrations, permissions and uncertain native interfaces are examples of such a risk.

rules.rule: A spec review of the contract before any code needs one short concrete risk reason, recorded in the contract.

units.text: Required G/M, integration and release gates remain.

rules.rule: Required G/M, integration and release gates remain even when review is scaled.

units.text: The captain records one compact acceptance contract and points to its evidence.

rules.rule: The captain records one compact acceptance contract and points to its evidence.

units.text: A map-holder-held ticket is run directly by the map holder whose map it clears; it receives no captain, branch, PR or review loop.

rules.rule: A map-holder-held ticket is run directly by the map holder whose map it clears.
A map-holder-held ticket receives no captain, branch, PR or review loop.

units.text: `Task` names the captain-held ticket's role on a map; it is not a label.

rules.rule: `Task` names the captain-held ticket's role on a map; it is not a label.

units.text: Small lookups, conversations and setup stay on the ticket that needs them.

rules.rule: Small lookups, conversations and setup stay on the ticket that needs them.

units.text: Create a map-holder-held ticket only when the work needs independent tracking or blocks other work.

rules.rule: Create a map-holder-held ticket only when the work needs independent tracking or blocks other work.

units.text: | `AFK` | The captain reaches reviewed completion without a live conversation. An unexpected choice for the user becomes a blocking `Question`; the parent stays AFK. | `#30A46C` |

rules.rule: Mode `AFK`: the captain reaches reviewed completion without a live conversation.
On an AFK ticket an unexpected choice for the user becomes a blocking `Question`, and the parent stays AFK.

units.text: | `HITL` | The user and the captain work the ticket together in a session the user opened. | `#F76B15` |

rules.rule: Mode `HITL`: the user and the captain work the ticket together in a session the user opened.

units.text: The user's approval or inspection at a universal gate does not make a ticket HITL.

rules.rule: The user's approval or inspection at a universal gate does not make a ticket HITL.

units.text: A ticket born from a finding carries that finding's severity, by DR 058's names; whoever files the ticket sets it.

rules.rule: A ticket born from a finding carries that finding's severity, by DR 058's names.
Whoever files a ticket born from a finding sets its Severity.

units.text: Most tickets carry none.

rules.rule: Most tickets carry no Severity.

units.text: | `blocker` | The intended case is wrong. | each blocker Bug an inquisition files | `#E5484D` |

rules.rule: Severity `blocker` (the intended case is wrong) is carried by each blocker Bug an inquisition files.

units.text: | `should` | A real bug callers will hit, inside the intent. | each should ticket filed from a review; each should Bug an inquisition files | `#FFB224` |

rules.rule: Severity `should` (a real bug callers will hit, inside the intent) is carried by each should ticket filed from a review and each should Bug an inquisition files.

units.text: | `nit` | Everything else. | each inquisition round's nit ticket | `#8B8D98` |

rules.rule: Severity `nit` (everything else) is carried by each inquisition round's nit ticket.

units.text: A review blocker stays a FAIL and never becomes a ticket; a review nit stays one line on its ticket's record.

rules.rule: A review blocker stays a FAIL and never becomes a ticket.
A review nit stays one line on its ticket's record.

units.text: Priority keeps its meaning and never carries severity.

rules.rule: Priority keeps its meaning and never carries severity.

units.text: The landing check is a query: no open `blocker` or `should` ticket in the Project, unless the user explicitly deferred it.

rules.rule: The landing check is a query: no open `blocker` or `should` ticket in the Project, unless the user explicitly deferred it.

units.text: Priority is the user's hint for which of his tickets to take next, so that the one unlocking the most AFK work goes first.

notRule.note: why Priority exists: the user takes first the ticket unlocking the most AFK work

units.text: The map holder sets it on every ticket that waits on the user, a `Question` or a HITL ticket, and re-sets it as blockers change.

rules.rule: The map holder sets Priority on every ticket that waits on the user (a `Question` or a HITL ticket) and re-sets it as blockers change.

units.text: | `Urgent` | An emergency; never set by default. |

rules.rule: Priority `Urgent` means an emergency and is never set by default.

units.text: | `High` | Clearing it lets a top-level ticket, or a Project's next step, run AFK. |

rules.rule: Priority `High` is set when clearing the ticket lets a top-level ticket, or a Project's next step, run AFK.

units.text: | `Medium` | Clearing it lets a lane run AFK. |

rules.rule: Priority `Medium` is set when clearing the ticket lets a lane run AFK.

units.text: | `Low` | Nothing runs AFK when it clears; the user must clear it anyway. |

rules.rule: Priority `Low` is set when nothing runs AFK on clearing but the user must clear it anyway.

units.text: AFK tickets carry no priority: the plan order and the native blockers carry their sequence.

rules.rule: AFK tickets carry no priority; the plan order and the native blockers carry their sequence.

units.text: The map holder is the user, or an admiral the user invoked, for a Project, and the captain for a ticket; the Project description names the Project's current holder.

rules.rule: The map holder is the user, or an admiral the user invoked, for a Project, and the captain for a ticket.
The Project description names the Project's current holder.

units.text: The map holder writes the contracts one level down, charts with `wayfinder` before dividing, and runs the map-holder-held tickets that clear its own fog: it dispatches `research`, runs a Grilling or Walkthrough with the user, and files a `Question` only when judgment remains.

rules.rule: The map holder writes the contracts one level down.
The map holder charts with `wayfinder` before dividing.
The map holder runs the map-holder-held tickets that clear its own fog: it dispatches `research`, runs a Grilling or Walkthrough with the user, and files a `Question` only when judgment remains.

units.text: | `Research` | `Todo` → `In Progress` → `Done` |

rules.rule: A `Research` ticket's normal status path is `Todo` -> `In Progress` -> `Done`.

units.text: | `Grilling`, `Walkthrough` | `Todo` → `In Progress` → `Done` |

rules.rule: A `Grilling` or `Walkthrough` ticket's normal status path is `Todo` -> `In Progress` -> `Done`.

units.text: | `Question` | `Todo` → `Done` |

rules.rule: A `Question` ticket's normal status path is `Todo` -> `Done`.

units.text: | `Inquisition` | `Backlog` → `Todo`, the user's confirmation → `In Progress`, the commission inputs, area map, phases, triage and patch lane → `Implementing` → `In Review` → `Ready to Merge` → `Done`, its record's docs chain. It releases to `Todo` with `released <key>: verification skill first`, resuming once the skill exists, or with `released <key>: groups <keys>`, resuming `In Progress` once its group Sub-tickets, each `Todo` → `In Progress` → `Done`, close; follow the [working-tree standard](../guides/working-tree-standard.md#retaining-an-inquisitions-record-and-proofs) |

rules.rule: An `Inquisition` ticket's normal status path is `Backlog` -> `Todo` (the user's confirmation) -> `In Progress` (the commission inputs, area map, phases, triage and patch lane) -> `Implementing` -> `In Review` -> `Ready to Merge` -> `Done`, its record's docs chain.

An Inquisition releases to `Todo` with `released <key>: verification skill first`, resuming once the skill exists, or with `released <key>: groups <keys>`, resuming `In Progress` once its group Sub-tickets (each `Todo` -> `In Progress` -> `Done`) close.
An Inquisition follows the working-tree standard on retaining its record and proofs.

units.text: | captain-held default, subject to the Type exceptions | `Todo` → `Implementing` → `In Review` → `Ready to Merge` → `Done`, with `In Progress` while lanes run |

rules.rule: A captain-held ticket's default status path, subject to the Type exceptions, is `Todo` -> `Implementing` -> `In Review` -> `Ready to Merge` -> `Done`, with `In Progress` while lanes run.

units.text: | Merge Sub-ticket | `Todo` → `Implementing` → `In Review` → `Done`; it merges, it is never merged |

rules.rule: A Merge Sub-ticket's status path is `Todo` -> `Implementing` -> `In Review` -> `Done`; it merges and is never merged.

units.text: A Project's map holder places its Milestones in Linear while charting: few, each a meaningful chunk of work where a drift from the user's intent would show, the walking skeleton first and the landing last.

rules.rule: A Project's map holder places its Milestones in Linear while charting: few, each a meaningful chunk of work where a drift from the user's intent would show, the walking skeleton first and the landing last.

units.text: Every delivery ticket belongs to one, and each Milestone has one Walkthrough Ticket.

rules.rule: Every delivery ticket belongs to one Milestone.
Each Milestone has one Walkthrough Ticket.

units.text: Only the walking skeleton's holds back the work built on it: filed with the map, it is a native blocker of the next Milestone's delivery tickets until his verdict or skip closes it.

rules.rule: Only the walking skeleton's Walkthrough Ticket holds back later work: filed with the map, it is a native blocker of the next Milestone's delivery tickets until the user's verdict or skip closes it.

units.text: In overnight mode it blocks nothing, and later Milestones' Walkthrough Tickets never block.

rules.rule: In overnight mode the walking skeleton's Walkthrough Ticket blocks nothing.
Later Milestones' Walkthrough Tickets never block.

units.text: A captain creates Sub-tickets one level deep: lanes for separate work that can run at the same time, each carrying its parent's Type and Mode, a Merge Sub-ticket for each merge operation except an atomic ticket's own merge into main, which the user clicks once its PR carries a reviewer PASS and CI is green, and a map-holder-held Sub-ticket for fog that blocks only its parent or a lane and stays inside the approved Project destination and ticket outcome.

rules.rule: A captain creates Sub-tickets one level deep: lanes for separate work that can run at the same time, each carrying its parent's Type and Mode.
A captain creates a Merge Sub-ticket for each merge operation except an atomic ticket's own merge into main, which the user clicks once its PR carries a reviewer PASS and CI is green.
A captain creates a map-holder-held Sub-ticket for fog that blocks only its parent or a lane and stays inside the approved Project destination and ticket outcome.

units.text: A lane that needs splitting is replaced by sibling lanes.

rules.rule: A lane that needs splitting is replaced by sibling lanes.

units.text: When the answer can change other tickets, a shared contract, or the Project's destination, scope, acceptance criteria or governing architecture, the captain prepares the packet and the Project's map holder creates and wires the Project-level ticket.

rules.rule: When the answer can change other tickets, a shared contract, or the Project's destination, scope, acceptance criteria or governing architecture, the captain prepares the packet.
The Project's map holder creates and wires the Project-level ticket from the captain's packet.

units.text: Native blocker relations connect every waiting record to what it waits on.

rules.rule: Native blocker relations connect every waiting record to what it waits on.

units.text: The Bug Type template is a narrow exception to parallel delivery lanes: its captain may retain ordered reproduce-or-identify and fix Sub-tickets, with fix natively blocked by reproduction and shared paths transferred only after reproduction closes with its evidence recorded.

rules.rule: The Bug Type template is a narrow exception to parallel delivery lanes: its captain may retain ordered reproduce-or-identify and fix Sub-tickets, with fix natively blocked by reproduction.
Shared paths transfer to the fix Sub-ticket only after reproduction closes with its evidence recorded.

units.text: Each stage keeps the parent's Type and Mode and has its own contract, chain, branch and worktree; every actual integration has a Merge Sub-ticket.

rules.rule: Each Bug stage keeps the parent's Type and Mode and has its own contract, chain, branch and worktree.
Every actual integration has a Merge Sub-ticket.

units.text: For a simple Bug, collapse the staged placeholders into parent hops and close the unused records `Canceled` with the reason.

rules.rule: For a simple Bug, collapse the staged placeholders into parent hops and close the unused records `Canceled` with the reason.

units.text: Joining acceptance and final review stay on the parent; the exception creates no overlapping parallel ownership.

rules.rule: Joining acceptance and final review of a staged Bug stay on the parent.
The Bug-stage exception creates no overlapping parallel ownership.

units.text: A Question is the last step of discovery, not its substitute.

rules.rule: A Question is the last step of discovery, not its substitute.

units.text: Before creating one, search the governing Decision Records, Project plan, specifications, documentation, standards, code, tests and other authoritative sources; if they settle it, record the answer where the work lives and continue.

rules.rule: Before creating a Question, search the governing Decision Records, Project plan, specifications, documentation, standards, code, tests and other authoritative sources.
If those sources settle the question, record the answer where the work lives and continue instead of creating a Question.

units.text: Create the Question only when the user's judgment is still needed, in `Todo`, wired as a blocker of everything that waits.

rules.rule: Create the Question only when the user's judgment is still needed.
A Question is created in `Todo`, wired as a blocker of everything that waits.

units.text: Its body carries:

rules.rule: A Question ticket body carries four items: the one question; the named work it blocks and why; the sources searched and facts found; the credible options, trade-offs, and the recommendation when evidence supports one.

units.text: the one question;
the named work it blocks and why;
the sources searched and facts found;
the credible options, trade-offs, and the recommendation when evidence supports one.
If the answer determines which implementation ticket should exist, resolve the Question first.

rules.rule: If the answer determines which implementation ticket should exist, resolve the Question first.

units.text: A Question a `what-would-balazs-do` tribunal decided while the user was away, or on his own invocation, stays in `Todo` unwired, and work proceeds; he answers it with `RATIFIED` or `OVERTURNED`.

rules.rule: A Question a `what-would-balazs-do` tribunal decided while the user was away, or on his own invocation, stays in `Todo` unwired, and work proceeds.
The user answers a tribunal-decided Question with `RATIFIED` or `OVERTURNED`.

units.text: One Linear ticket template per Type, named after it, is a workspace-UI convenience.

notRule.note: one ticket template per Type exists as a workspace-UI convenience

units.text: Create it from the body below where the connected tools or UI permit.

rules.rule: Create a Linear ticket template from the body below where the connected tools or UI permit.

units.text: Agents read this standard and the ticket contract, then use the capabilities actually available; template listing or retrieval is not a required connector capability.

rules.rule: Agents read this standard and the ticket contract, then use the capabilities actually available; template listing or retrieval is not a required connector capability.

units.text: | `Feature` | `## Outcome` · `## Owned paths` · `## Blockers` · `## Exact gates` · `## Base branch`, plus optional `## Spec` linking relevant feature-spec sections: the captain's bounded acceptance contract; `## Exact gates` names the command for each test, suite and static gate. |

rules.rule: A `Feature` ticket body has `## Outcome`, `## Owned paths`, `## Blockers`, `## Exact gates`, `## Base branch`, plus optional `## Spec` linking feature-spec sections; it is the captain's bounded acceptance contract, and `## Exact gates` names the command for each test, suite and static gate.

units.text: | `Bug` | the five fields, then `## Observed`, `## Expected`, `## Reproduction` (a scenario at the boundary, else the red test; a prose Bug quotes both contradicting passages at `file:line`; an unused member, export or field quotes its definition at `file:line` and a reference search showing no caller outside the tests); default Sub-tickets: *reproduce or identify*, *fix*. |

rules.rule: A `Bug` ticket body has the five fields, then `## Observed`, `## Expected`, `## Reproduction` (a scenario at the boundary, else the red test; a prose Bug quotes both contradicting passages at `file:line`; an unused member, export or field quotes its definition at `file:line` and a reference search showing no caller outside the tests), with default Sub-tickets reproduce-or-identify and fix.

units.text: | `Merge` | `## Source` and `## Target` at their SHAs, `## Plan order` (the Merge Sub-ticket this one is blocked by), `## Combined gates`, `## Conflicts expected`. |

rules.rule: A `Merge` ticket body has `## Source` and `## Target` at their SHAs, `## Plan order` (the Merge Sub-ticket this one is blocked by), `## Combined gates`, `## Conflicts expected`.

units.text: | `Enablement` | `## Condition` that must become true, `## Steps only the user can do`, `## Evidence` when done. |

rules.rule: An `Enablement` ticket body has `## Condition` that must become true, `## Steps only the user can do`, and `## Evidence` when done.

units.text: | `Inquisition` | `## Scope`: the commission inputs - the audit SHA, the integrated feature commit and the landing base, the governing intent, a provider and model per phase and the swarm width, the Codex cap, the crew context limit, and the verification skill or why nothing runs; `## Area map`, drawn fresh each round; `## Findings`, the register's link and each finding's disposition: Bugs, patches, the nit ticket, Questions; `## Record` path. The round's nit ticket is a `Feature`, Mode `AFK`, `Backlog`, held by the map holder and linked to its Inquisition; it is listed at the Project's final walkthrough, where the user decides each nit, and closes `Done` once every nit is fixed or accepted as is. |

rules.rule: An `Inquisition` ticket body has `## Scope` (the commission inputs: audit SHA, integrated feature commit and landing base, governing intent, provider and model per phase and swarm width, Codex cap, crew context limit, and the verification skill or why nothing runs), `## Area map` drawn fresh each round, `## Findings` (the register's link and each finding's disposition), and `## Record` path.
The round's nit ticket is a `Feature`, Mode `AFK`, `Backlog`, held by the map holder and linked to its Inquisition.
The nit ticket is listed at the Project's final walkthrough, where the user decides each nit, and closes `Done` once every nit is fixed or accepted as is.

units.text: | `Prototype` | `## Question` the sketch must settle, `## Variants`, `## Verdict` and the winning commit on `prototype/<name>`. |

rules.rule: A `Prototype` ticket body has `## Question` the sketch must settle, `## Variants`, `## Verdict` and the winning commit on `prototype/<name>`.

units.text: | `Question` | the four items above. |

rules.rule: A `Question` ticket body has the four items listed above.

units.text: | `Research` | `## Question` and `## Destination` for the cited report. |

rules.rule: A `Research` ticket body has `## Question` and `## Destination` for the cited report.

units.text: | `Grilling` | `## Subject` (the plan, decision or idea), `## Tree` of choices with their answers and reasoning, `## Records` linked. |

rules.rule: A `Grilling` ticket body has `## Subject`, `## Tree` of choices with their answers and reasoning, and `## Records` linked.

units.text: | `Walkthrough` | `## Checkpoint` (the Milestone or the landing, its branch and SHA), the four-part tour, `## Verdict` (his words, or the skip), `## Findings` as linked tickets. |

rules.rule: A `Walkthrough` ticket body has `## Checkpoint` (the Milestone or the landing, its branch and SHA), the four-part tour, `## Verdict` (the user's words, or the skip), and `## Findings` as linked tickets.

units.text: `## Exact gates` binds the [testing strategy](../guides/testing-strategy.md#feature-proof-and-gate-placement) to real project commands: selected own/reached features and parent-shared tests, Light/Heavy levels, prerequisites and stage, applicable static/mutation assurance, final coverage producer/consumer, and permitted evidence reuse.

rules.rule: `## Exact gates` binds the testing strategy to real project commands: selected own/reached features and parent-shared tests, Light/Heavy levels, prerequisites and stage, applicable static/mutation assurance, final coverage producer/consumer, and permitted evidence reuse.

units.text: List hop proof separately from final, combined-merge and release gates.

rules.rule: `## Exact gates` lists hop proof separately from final, combined-merge and release gates.

units.text: Name unavailable support and explicitly reconcile older active obligations; no gate is cancelled retrospectively by a new default.

rules.rule: `## Exact gates` names unavailable support and explicitly reconciles older active obligations.
No gate is cancelled retrospectively by a new default.

units.text: Use metadata first: the current active contract and named evidence only.

rules.rule: Use metadata first: read only the current active contract and named evidence.

units.text: Keep the stable current contract and state in the description.

rules.rule: Keep the stable current contract and state in the ticket description.

units.text: Read comments only for a named missing fact or binding review; comments have no assumed order.

rules.rule: Read comments only for a named missing fact or binding review; comments have no assumed order.

units.text: Filter tool output before it enters model context.

rules.rule: Filter tool output before it enters model context.

units.text: Name an agent without its `@` unless you mean to delegate: an `@mention` starts that agent's session.

rules.rule: Name an agent without its `@` unless you mean to delegate, because an `@mention` starts that agent's session.

units.text: Keep existing historical originals accessible.

rules.rule: Keep existing historical originals accessible.

units.text: Put new full raw proof and native gate logs once in a durable, linked Git or document artifact; do not dump them into PRs or comments.

rules.rule: Put new full raw proof and native gate logs once in a durable, linked Git or document artifact.
Do not dump full raw proof or gate logs into PRs or comments.

units.text: Each gate result names its candidate, command, environment or session, exit and result location.

rules.rule: Each gate result names its candidate, command, environment or session, exit and result location.

units.text: Before expensive tests, record cheap proof of repository or snapshot, intended selection and nonzero discovery; a quiet healthy test continues.

rules.rule: Before expensive tests, record cheap proof of repository or snapshot, intended selection and nonzero discovery; a quiet healthy test continues.

units.text: Reuse exact-candidate evidence only when the gate and environment permit it, rerunning after relevant changes or new concerns and at mandatory integration or release boundaries.

rules.rule: Reuse exact-candidate evidence only when the gate and environment permit it, rerunning after relevant changes or new concerns and at mandatory integration or release boundaries.

units.text: Ticket-and-PR binding review stays compact but complete.

rules.rule: Ticket-and-PR binding review stays compact but complete.

units.text: Ordinary updates expose only counts, exits, failure excerpts, and an evidence link.

rules.rule: Ordinary updates expose only counts, exits, failure excerpts, and an evidence link.

units.text: Do not repeat contracts, hashes, full returns, passing-test name dumps, unchanged updates, or token, cost, or latency claims.

rules.rule: Do not repeat contracts, hashes, full returns, passing-test name dumps, unchanged updates, or token, cost, or latency claims.

units.text: Review gates stay where their workflows require.

rules.rule: Review gates stay where their workflows require.

units.text: Start each post with the applicable form:

rules.rule: Start each Linear post with the applicable form (PASS, FAIL, IMPLEMENTED, DECIDED, RATIFIED, OVERTURNED, STATE).

units.text: `PASS - rubric/type: <rubric>; contract <ref>; candidate <SHA>; base <SHA>; reviewer/model: <name>; applicable tests <N/N>, gates <N/N>. Checks: <one substantive sentence>. Deferred (optional): 1. Where: <place>; severity: <should|nit>; wrong: <fact>; why: <impact>; required correction: <action>; owner: <role>. Evidence: <link>.`

rules.rule: A PASS block reads `PASS - rubric/type: <rubric>; contract <ref>; candidate <SHA>; base <SHA>; reviewer/model: <name>; applicable tests <N/N>, gates <N/N>. Checks: <one substantive sentence>. Deferred (optional): 1. Where; severity: <should|nit>; wrong; why; required correction; owner. Evidence: <link>.`

units.text: `FAIL - rubric/type: <rubric>; contract <ref>; candidate <SHA>; base <SHA>; reviewer/model: <name>; gates <N/N>. 1. Where: <place>; severity: <blocker|should|nit>; wrong: <fact>; why: <impact>; required correction: <action>; owner: <role>. Evidence: <link>.`

rules.rule: A FAIL block reads `FAIL - rubric/type: <rubric>; contract <ref>; candidate <SHA>; base <SHA>; reviewer/model: <name>; gates <N/N>. 1. Where; severity: <blocker|should|nit>; wrong; why; required correction; owner. Evidence: <link>.`

units.text: `IMPLEMENTED - hop/candidate <SHA>; <behavior>; proof: <evidence>; blocker: <none or named blocker>.`

rules.rule: An IMPLEMENTED return reads `IMPLEMENTED - hop/candidate <SHA>; <behavior>; proof: <evidence>; blocker: <none or named blocker>.`

units.text: `DECIDED - result: <result>; immutable contract: <contract>; next: <action>.`

rules.rule: A DECIDED block reads `DECIDED - result: <result>; immutable contract: <contract>; next: <action>.`

units.text: `DECIDED - by: what-would-balazs-do tribunal, unratified; result: <action>; vote: <n of 3, or split; most reversible>; log: <link>; undo: <steps>; next: <action>.`

rules.rule: A tribunal DECIDED block reads `DECIDED - by: what-would-balazs-do tribunal, unratified; result: <action>; vote: <n of 3, or split; most reversible>; log: <link>; undo: <steps>; next: <action>.`

units.text: `RATIFIED - by: <the user> <date>: "<his words, verbatim>"; record: <DECIDED or DR link>; next: <action>.`

rules.rule: A RATIFIED block reads `RATIFIED - by: <the user> <date>: "<his words, verbatim>"; record: <DECIDED or DR link>; next: <action>.`

units.text: `OVERTURNED - by: <the user> <date>: "<his words, verbatim>"; record: <link>; reopened: <tickets>; next: <action>.`

rules.rule: An OVERTURNED block reads `OVERTURNED - by: <the user> <date>: "<his words, verbatim>"; record: <link>; reopened: <tickets>; next: <action>.`

units.text: `STATE - <status>; owner: <role>; candidate or PR: <reference>; next or blocker: <fact>; evidence: <link>.`

rules.rule: A STATE block reads `STATE - <status>; owner: <role>; candidate or PR: <reference>; next or blocker: <fact>; evidence: <link>.`

units.text: A review block's `contract <ref>` is the contract its brief pinned, for a ticket `<KEY> description as of <Linear updatedAt>`; `base <SHA>` is the brief's base.

rules.rule: A review block's `contract <ref>` is the contract its brief pinned, for a ticket `<KEY> description as of <Linear updatedAt>`.
A review block's `base <SHA>` is the brief's base.

units.text: A FAIL carries at least one blocker; a PASS carries none and lists its should and nit findings under `Deferred`.

rules.rule: A FAIL carries at least one blocker.
A PASS carries no blocker and lists its should and nit findings under `Deferred`.

units.text: The captain files each should as its own ticket and records each nit as one line on the record.

rules.rule: The captain files each should as its own ticket.
The captain records each nit as one line on the record.

units.text: Brevity is soft: ordinary events aim for at most 800 characters, descriptions and state for at most 1,500 characters or 12 lines.

rules.rule: Brevity is soft: ordinary events aim for at most 800 characters; descriptions and state for at most 1,500 characters or 12 lines.

units.text: A necessary finding, gap, blocker, or evidence may exceed those aims; omit narration and repetition either way.

rules.rule: A necessary finding, gap, blocker, or evidence may exceed the length aims; omit narration and repetition either way.

units.text: A writer's successful delivery is never an independent `PASS`.

rules.rule: A writer's successful delivery is never an independent `PASS`.

units.text: Every agent-authored Linear comment identifies its acting role and truthful model identity.

rules.rule: Every agent-authored Linear comment identifies its acting role and truthful model identity.

units.text: State the effective identity when trustworthy runtime information exposes it.

rules.rule: State the effective model identity when trustworthy runtime information exposes it.

units.text: Otherwise qualify a family or a requested/configured value; never infer an alias resolution, parent model, or effort.

rules.rule: When the effective identity is not exposed, qualify a family or a requested/configured value.
Never infer an alias resolution, parent model, or effort.

units.text: State effort only when it is known and useful.

rules.rule: State effort only when it is known and useful.

units.text: A captain relay preserves the original author or reviewer identity and distinguishes the captain's posting identity.

rules.rule: A captain relay preserves the original author or reviewer identity and distinguishes the captain's posting identity.

units.text: The reviewer field in a reviewer block is its signature, so do not add a second or conflicting one.

rules.rule: The reviewer field in a reviewer block is its signature; do not add a second or conflicting one.

units.text: Historical comments stay untouched.

rules.rule: Historical comments stay untouched.

units.text: Examples:
`IMPLEMENTED - hop/candidate <SHA>; docs-writer/model: gpt-5.6-terra; proof: <evidence>; blocker: none.`

`PASS - rubric/type: docs; contract <ref>; candidate <SHA>; base <SHA>; reviewer/model: gpt-5.6-sol; applicable tests <N/N>, gates <N/N>. Checks: <one substantive sentence>. Evidence: <link>. posted by ticket-captain/model: gpt-5.6-terra.`

notRule.note: PASS block with captain-relay signature example

units.text: `IMPLEMENTED - hop/candidate <SHA>; docs-writer/model: gpt-5.6-luna (later task); proof: <evidence>; blocker: none.`

notRule.note: IMPLEMENTED signature with later-task model example

units.text: `STATE - Implementing; owner: code-writer; requested model: gpt-5.6-terra (effective identity unavailable); next: <fact>; evidence: <link>.`

notRule.note: STATE signature with requested model example

units.text: Linear records the decision-making work; dydo records a qualifying decision.

rules.rule: Linear records the decision-making work; dydo records a qualifying decision.

units.text: Link the Question or Grilling Ticket to its repository Decision Record and link the record back when it has a Linear origin.

rules.rule: Link the Question or Grilling Ticket to its repository Decision Record, and link the record back when it has a Linear origin.

units.text: The Decision Record is canonical: keep its rationale in dydo rather than copying it into Linear.

rules.rule: The Decision Record is canonical: keep its rationale in dydo rather than copying it into Linear.
